finding.headline: You plan to retire at 62, so you would need your own health coverage for 3 years before Medicare at 65.
details: Medicare generally starts when you turn 65, and your sign-up window runs 3 months before to 3 months after that month. If you miss that window, you may wait and pay a monthly late penalty that grows the longer you wait.
Social Security can start as early as 62, but you get full benefits only at full retirement age. The benefit increase from delaying stops at 70.

assumptions: All figures are in today's dollars: what money buys now, not the larger sums prices will reach.

Savings grow on average 5.0% a year above inflation in stocks and 1.8% in bonds, with good and bad years. The plan tests many possible market paths. These are planning figures, not a forecast. They are fixed, so every plan is tested on the same markets; to see a bad stretch, try a What If such as markets fall 30%.
Your spending now is about $5,174 a year more than your take-home pay, so until you retire the plan takes that from your savings each year. If that is wrong, change your spending now or your pay.
Pay stays at today's level until you retire, with no raises. This is fixed: raises are not certain, so the plan does not count on them. If your pay changes, change it in your answers.
Social Security uses the figure you gave, read as the benefit at 67. Your answers show $7,500 a year from 67. This plan starts it at 62, which pays about $5,200 a year.
If you retire before Medicare starts at 65, health cover costs about $10,000 a person a year until then (an assumption). Other health costs follow CMS figures by age.

Tax uses the 2027 federal brackets, the standard deduction and your state's rates. While you work, 401(k) saving comes off taxable pay. In retirement the plan counts 85% of Social Security as taxable, the most the law allows, so the tax may be a little high.
The plan runs to age 96. There is about a 1 in 4 chance that you will live that long (US life table, SOA 2024). People with more money tend to live longer than that table says.
